Major duties include but are not limited to: Responsible for administrative and strategic direction of the supply chain, to include budget execution, for VISN-wide logistical programs.

Oversees and manages strategic planning, auditing, quality assurance, and program compliance and oversight of all SCM programs and inspections as well as various activities designed to enhance the mission of the affected VISN and its facilities.

Identifies all activities involved supporting the needs of supply chain, including capital asset planning, lifecycle management of equipment, strategic sourcing of commodities such as clinical supplies, maintenance supplies and service, subsistence, medical gases, and durable medical equipment and services for inpatient and inpatient services home care.

Conducts Supply Chain audits, compliance reviews, and program effectiveness/efficiency reviews based on self-developed and nationally developed standards of all VISN facilities.

Maintain VISN supply chain program standards by establishing a training program, developing a curriculum, creating training opportunities, and developing standard tests designed to enhance the skills and abilities of their Medical Center's supply chain staff.

Mentor and guide Facility Chief Supply Chain Officers (FCSCOs), and other VISN and facility Supply Chain personnel, including interns resulting from the National Logistics and Acquisition Training Programs. Oversee delegated purchasing authority within the purchase card program for all clinical supply and equipment items.

Assists with acquisition support activities and the acquisition staff with Advanced Procurement Planning (APP), evaluating products and services for award, championing the use of standardized products through management of awarded contracts, ensuring receipt documentation is properly executed for payment, facilitating achievement of socio-economic program goals, and leveraging the VA's influence in the healthcare marketplace.

Manages multi-million dollar budgets for staff training, equipment (both capital and non-capital), assigned staff salaries, and special projects.

Directs the VISN supply chain management operations that involve planning, coordinating, and evaluating Supply Chain actions required to support VHA's operational readiness efforts and Regional Readiness Center (RRC) program. Provides direct supervision to employees performing various duties supporting the Supply Chain Program throughout the VISN.

Work Schedule: Monday - Friday, 7:30am - 4:00pm Telework: This position may be authorized for Ad-hoc telework. Telework eligibility will be discussed during the interview process. Virtual: This is not a virtual position.

Lambda is seeking a highly motivated and hands-on Supply Chain Systems & Process Lead to drive the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of business processes across Supply Chain, Procurement, Operations, and Finance.
This role will serve as the bridge between business teams and system implementations, ensuring processes are scalable, standardized, and effectively enabled through systems such as NetSuite, Coupa, PLM, Asset Management, and related operational tools.
The ideal candidate combines strong business process knowledge with systems expertise and has a proven ability to drive initiatives from requirements gathering through implementation and adoption.

Supply Chain Systems & Process Transformation
Evaluate current-state business processes and identify opportunities for automation, standardization, and operational efficiency.
Design and implement scalable workflows across Supply Chain, Procurement, Materials Management, Asset Management, and Financial Operations.
Develop business requirements, process maps, SOPs, and governance frameworks.
Drive adoption and continuous improvement of implemented solutions.
Systems Ownership & Implementation
Partner with Business Systems, Engineering, Finance, and Operations teams to implement and optimize business systems.
Lead process design and implementation efforts across NetSuite, Coupa, PLM, Asset Management, and related platforms.

Improve procurement workflows, approval structures, and reporting capabilities.
Partner with Finance and Accounting to improve spend visibility, cost tracking, invoice workflows, and GL alignment.
Drive process improvements across procurement, vendor management, and operational spending.
Master Data & Process Governance
Support Item Master, BOM, and Product Lifecycle Management initiatives.
Establish governance around master data, approvals, and change management processes.
Improve data quality, process compliance, and operational controls.
Cross-Functional Leadership
Facilitate workshops and working sessions across Supply Chain, Finance, Accounting, Operations, PMO, Data Center Infrastructure Engineering (DCIE), and Business Systems teams.
Drive alignment, decision-making, and execution across multiple stakeholders.
Identify risks, dependencies, and process gaps while developing practical solutions.
Reporting & Operational Excellence
Develop and track process performance metrics.
Analyze operational data to identify trends, bottlenecks, and improvement opportunities.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives that improve scalability, efficiency, and visibility across the organization.

7+ years of experience in Supply Chain, Procurement, Business Systems, Operations Excellence, or Process Transformation.

The Director of Supply Chain Strategy & Excellence is a high-impact leadership role responsible for architecting and executing a comprehensive end-to-end supply chain strategy. This position focuses on driving operational excellence, long-term scalability, and rigorous cost management across the enterprise.

The successful candidate will use advanced SQL and Python to build rigorous data models, surface operational insights to craft a strategic vision, identify opportunities to deploy advanced AI-driven technologies to automate decision-making and improve predictive accuracy, and optimize the global network to enhance service levels and deliver significant bottom-line value.

Develop and implement a multi-year supply chain roadmap aligned with corporate growth and fiscal objectives
Network Design: Lead the design and optimization of the global distribution and logistics network to ensure maximum efficiency and customer satisfaction
Serve as a key advisor to executive leadership on supply chain trends, risks, and investment opportunities
Drive cross-functional alignment between Finance, Operations, Sales, and Marketing to ensure integrated business planning
Targeted Savings: Establish and manage robust cost-reduction programs targeting delivery, service & repair, refurbishment, and transportation
Cost of Quality (CoQ): Drive "Quality-by-Design" initiatives, incorporating member and engineering feedback to optimize product reliability and reduce total CoQ
Oversee the supply chain budget, ensuring financial targets are met through rigorous expense management and productivity gains
Implement total landed cost models to drive data-driven decision-making in sourcing and logistics
Partner with analytics engineering to define and build dbt data models that translate exploratory supply chain analyses into reliable, reusable data infrastructure
AI Deployment: Incorporate AI tools into analytical workflows and build AI-assisted data capabilities that empower non-technical supply chain partners to make faster, better decisions
Member First Analytics: Use data to develop feedback loops to drive continuous improvement of the member experience
Develop and monitor KPIs focused on cost-to-serve, perfect order fulfillment, and working capital efficiency
Champion a culture of continuous improvement utilizing Lean or Six Sigma methodologies to eliminate waste
Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing team, focusing on increasing internal talent density
Promote a data-driven mindset and technical proficiency across the department
Define organizational structures and roles that support evolving business needs and scalability
Foster a culture of high performance with a focus on retention of top talent
Bachelor’s Degree: Required in Supply Chain Management, Operations, Engineering, Finance, or a related field

8+ years of progressive leadership experience in supply chain, logistics, or operations, with a proven track record of delivering cost-savings and strategic transformations
Advanced SQL and Python proficiency with hands-on experience building models and conducting deep-dive analyses
Exceptional ability to interpret complex data sets and translate them into actionable strategic insights
Ability to see the big picture while maintaining attention to detail in execution
Strong executive presence with the ability to influence stakeholders at all levels of the organization
Experience with dbt or modern analytics engineering workflows, including defining data models and working with engineering teams to productionize analytical work — strongly preferred
Experience incorporating AI tools into personal data workflows and helping non-technical teams adopt AI-assisted approaches
Demonstrated success in leading large-scale organizational change initiatives
Success Metrics
Total Landed Cost Reduction - Target Goal: Annual target of 5-8% reduction across primary categories
Inventory Turnover - Target Goal: Improvement of 10% year-over-year
On-Time-In-Full (OTIF) - Target Goal: Achieve and maintain >98%
Forecast Accuracy - Target Goal: Improvement of 20% through integrated planning

Reviews complex and novel logistics and supply chain management issues and develops new methods, processes or techniques to address these. Evaluates evolving technology in the field and determines the best use of technology to accomplish logistics program objectives. Accounts for the integration and alignment of acquisition, delivery and management of supplies, equipment and services to ensure the successful delivery of patient care.

Oversees the execution of standardized business processes, established performance measures and analyzes the supply chain, developing actions as a result of analysis results, metrics, quality assurance/compliance, operating practices, and reporting within the facility.

Supports the coordination and integration of new technology and/or implementation of new supply/equipment requirements. Serves as expert logistician for the CSCO.

Integrates operations for the acquisition and procurement of complex healthcare resources that involve planning, coordinating, and evaluating the logistical and supply chain management actions required to support the complex requirements of a large healthcare system.

Oversees, guides, manages, and integrates supply chain operations across the facility/organizations; plans/coordinates with fiscal, acquisition, clinical and administrative operations.

Provides expert input with direction of supply chain, budget projections/execution for logistics programs and contracts, and in VISN financial, business, capital asset management, clinical, and administrative operations.

Serves as a senior VA HCS logistics expert and utilizes extensive knowledge of supply chain systems and requirements and provides direct support to the VA HCS, multiple campuses, and support catchment areas; provides expert level technical advice and guidance to all organizational logistics personnel pertaining to logistics.

Performs broad and comprehensive formal studies of benefits, impacts, characteristics and problems associated with logistics policy. Analyzes the supply chain, developing actions as a result of analysis results, metrics, quality assurance/compliance, operating practices, and reporting within the health care system.

Develops performance measurement/management of all of the aforementioned (including statistical analysis, workload projections, and process management). Analyzes and coordinates information and requirements with the facility, VISN and VACO in the area of acquisitions and procurement, supply, equipment and medical readiness.

Through subordinate managers, conducts cost-benefit analysis for procurements through the total supply chain. Analyzes supply status and directs the priority of maintenance effort for organizational equipment. Provides technical expert input to CSCO, establishes policy and ensures best practices are implemented as appropriate, utilizing continuous quality improvement principles, practices and initiatives, including six sigma and lean management.

To qualify for this position, applicants must meet all requirements by the closing date of this announcement, 07/27/2026. Time-In-Grade Requirement: Applicants who are current Federal employees and have held a GS grade any time in the past 52 weeks must also meet time-in-grade requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

For a GS-13 position you must have served 52 weeks at the GS-12. The grade may have been in any occupation, but must have been held in the Federal service. An SF-50 that shows your time-in-grade eligibility must be submitted with your application materials.

If the most recent SF-50 has an effective date within the past year, it may not clearly demonstrate you possess one-year time-in-grade, as required by the announcement. In this instance, you must provide an additional SF-50 that clearly demonstrates one-year time-in-grade.

You may qualify based on your experience as described below: Specialized Experience: You must have one year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the next lower grade GS-12 in the normal line of progression for the occupation in the organization.

Examples of specialized experience would typically include, but are not limited to: serving as a supply chain management leader/supervisor; ensuring the logistical requirements of an organization are met; planning/coordinating and evaluating various operations of a logistics program; providing acquisition management, purchasing, transportation, distribution, inventory management and control, expendable and non-expendable equipment, and warehouse operations; assisting with budget formulation and forecasting of expenditures; and managing a group with a variety of occupations and subordinate supervisors.

Place purchase orders to allocated vendors for a variety of food or packaging Stock Keeping Units (SKUs), at the correct price, quantity, buffer, etc.
Partner with HelloFresh distribution centers, offsite production and warehouse locations, and suppliers to ensure timely deliveries and inventories match demand requirements

With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

Shield AI is building the world’s best AI pilot. Our autonomous systems, including V-BAT and Hivemind Enterprise, operate in the most contested environments in the world. As next-generation aircraft programs transition from development into production, operational agility and production discipline are critical to delivering mission-ready systems while enabling rapid innovation.
We are seeking a Senior Production Planner for Development Programs to drive production planning and execution for developmental and prototype aircraft builds. This role operates at the intersection of Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain, and Program Management to ensure aircraft build schedules remain executable despite evolving designs, changing priorities, and material constraints.

The Senior Production Planner – Development Programs is responsible for developing, maintaining, and executing production plans for prototype and developmental aircraft programs. Unlike traditional production environments, this role must navigate incomplete engineering definition, evolving bills of material, shifting program priorities, and dynamic supply chain conditions while maintaining progress toward key build and flight test milestones.
You will serve as a critical coordination point between Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, and Program Management to translate rapidly changing program requirements into actionable production plans.

Develop and maintain detailed production schedules for prototype aircraft builds, major assemblies, and integration activities
Translate engineering release plans, build priorities, and program milestones into executable manufacturing schedules
Release and manage work orders in support of aircraft builds, including builds with incomplete engineering definition or evolving configurations or bills of material
Coordinate schedule adjustments resulting from engineering changes, design revisions, and shifting program priorities
Monitor production progress and proactively identify risks to key build, integration, and flight test milestones
Coordinate temporary planning structures and workarounds to enable manufacturing progress while maintaining configuration control
Facilitate rapid schedule recovery plans when design, material, or technical issues affect build progress
Partner closely with Supply Chain to align material availability with build requirements and timelines
Support ERP/MRP system accuracy through effective planning and work order management

Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, or related field
5+ years of experience in production planning, manufacturing planning, production control, or supply chain operations
Experience supporting complex hardware, aerospace, defense, automotive, robotics, or other highly engineered products
Experience working within ERP/MRP systems (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, Costpoint, or similar)
Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, work order management, bills of material, and production scheduling
Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced and highly dynamic environment
U.S. citizenship and ability to obtain/maintain a security clearance

Experience supporting prototype, NPI (New Product Introduction), or developmental manufacturing programs
Experience in UAV, aerospace, defense, or aircraft production environments
Familiarity with engineering change management and configuration control processes
APICS CPIM certification

At Shield AI, prototype aircraft builds are where innovation becomes reality. Every developmental aircraft completed advances the future of autonomous aviation and accelerates mission capability for our customers.
This role sits at the center of that effort, helping transform evolving designs into flight-ready aircraft while building the production foundation for future scale.
If you are excited about solving complex manufacturing challenges and enabling next-generation autonomous aircraft programs, we want to hear from you.
Join us in building the world's best AI pilot.

Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.
Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.
We are looking for a Senior Logistics Manager, Americas Retail Operations to act as the definitive leader for all things retail logistics within the Americas.

Oura is experiencing explosive momentum, delivering 100% YoY growth over the past three years—moving from zero retailers in 2023 to multiple active major accounts today, with more launches slated for this year alone.

In this role, you will lead a team of 2 direct reports and take full scope ownership of both sustaining/optimizing our current retail footprint and executing flawless new retailer launches.

You will own the performance metrics, drive cost-down strategies, and act as the vital bridge between retail operations, 3PL partners, and our internal Trade and Logistics teams.
This is a hybrid role onsite 2-3x per week in SF
Sustaining & Launch Operations
Act as the primary logistics operational lead for all Americas retail channels, ensuring existing accounts are optimized while seamlessly onboarding the 6 new retailers in our pipeline.
Evaluate complex new retailer routing guides and technical requirements, setting up our 3PL partners successfully to execute error-free launches.
Enforce strict compliance across routing guides, packaging/labeling mandates, and technical EDI readiness to protect brand reputation and delivery standards.
Drive operational efficiency to systematically accelerate fulfillment speed and shorten PO-to-delivery timeframes across the Americas.
Financial Performance & Compliance Analysis
Run sophisticated cost analyses across both Prepaid and Collect freight models to determine the most profitable distribution path forward and map out our true cost-to-serve.
Create, implement, and own an end-to-end chargeback deduction and dispute process to rigorously defend company margins against retail penalties.
Identify, analyze, and execute aggressive logistics cost-down initiatives to reduce total retail cost-per-unit.
Own all retail KPI reporting and performance analysis, turning operational data into actionable supply chain improvements.
Cross-Functional & Network Collaboration
Serve as the definitive cross-functional voice for logistics, partnering closely with Sales and Account Management during commercial expansion discussions to ensure supply chain readiness.
Collaborate closely with internal Trade Compliance and Global Logistics teams to design and align the warehouse and distribution networks needed to support further expansions into Canada and LATAM.
Partner with technical and IT teams to automate manual tracking workflows, reduce data errors, and enhance real-time end-to-end shipment visibility.
Leadership & Team Development
Directly manage, train, and mentor a dedicated team of two current logistics reports, fostering their professional development.
Define the long-term operational blueprint, scaling strategy, and structure for what the Americas retail logistics team looks like down the line.

s.h: We would love to consider you for this role if you have

7+ years of experience in retail logistics, B2B wholesale distribution, or supply chain operations, including 2+ years of direct people management experience within a product-shipping industry (e.g., CPG, Consumer Electronics, Apparel).
Deep technical expertise in retail compliance and chargeback management, with a proven track record of analyzing routing guides, managing EDI setups, and building systematic processes to audit and dispute retailer deductions.
Strong financial and operational analytical skills, specifically experienced in running freight cost-to-serve models, evaluating Prepaid vs. Collect structures, and optimizing PO-to-delivery cycle times.
Collaborative network experience, with a background working closely alongside internal Trade Compliance and Global Logistics teams to support retail fulfillment nodes (exposure to Canada/LATAM distribution a plus).
Exceptional cross-functional communication and influence, with the ability to confidently act as the "voice of logistics" to sales teams, corporate leadership, and external 3PL partners.
High data literacy and a continuous-improvement mindset, capable of translating complex logistics data into actionable workflow automation and aggressive cost-down strategies.

Wing ’s fleet of highly automated delivery drones can transport small packages directly from businesses to homes on-demand, in minutes. We design, build, and operate our aircraft, and offer drone delivery services on two continents.

Our technology is designed to be easy to integrate into existing delivery and logistics networks, offering a scalable drone delivery solution for a broad range of businesses. Wing is a part of Google's parent company, Alphabet, and our mission is to create the preferred means of delivery for the planet.

If you're ready to do the greatest work of your life, come join us.

Wing is looking for a Supply Chain Systems Manager to join our Manufacturing Operations team. This role is based remotely in the United States . As a Supply Chain Systems Analyst, you will be designing and providing solutions that enable supply chain functions for Wing ’s manufacturing, logistics and supply chain operations.

You will be the primary link between our physical drone production and our digital ecosystem, supporting a dynamic systems landscape spanning a group of tools and technologies.

You won't just be drawing diagrams, you will design the logic, write the requirements, and—when necessary— work alongside developers to solve supply chain business problems using industry best practices.

Design and implement supply chain system solutions using custom built and supply chain/enterprise systems (ERP, MRP, WMS, TMS, Data Visualization Tools) to enable manufacturing, logistics, inventory and supply chain operations
Lead and manage systems implementation projects, from business requirements definition through user acceptance testing and deployment into production use
Manage internal and external development programs to implement system solutions in alignment with the business plan
Drive cross-functional collaboration to architect robust data exchange (API/EDI) integrations between Wing ’s data systems and external partners, inclusive of manufacturing execution systems, inventory management systems, warehouse management systems, and MRP systems
Provide high fidelity business requirements documents and technical specs that allow development teams to execute with zero ambiguity

8+ years of hands-on experience designing and implementing supply chain systems. Strong knowledge of ERP systems (preferably SAP) and a proven ability to deliver efficient planning solutions in complex, global enterprise environments
Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience
Demonstrated experience building integrated systems throughout the entire life-cycle by designing and implementing Supply Chain systems, such as ERP, MRP, WMS, and TMS
Hands on experience with SAP S/4 HANA and customizing it for the business needs
Demonstrated ability to translate business requirements into effective solutions. Proven ability to lead IT-focused projects within a supply chain setting
Deep understanding of materials management, logistics (forward and reverse), inventory management, procurement, finance principles
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with experience working in global teams
Demonstrated ability to work in ambiguous environments and adapt to rapidly changing landscapes

Diva International Inc. (“DIVA”) is looking for a Sr. Supply Chain Specialist (12m Maternity Leave Contract) who will be responsible supporting inventory management, forecasting, supply chain operations, purchasing, assembly coordination, and internal quality control processes. This role provides analytical insight, operational support, and process improvements to ensure efficient production planning, inventory accuracy, and timely fulfillment across DIVA’s Canadian and U.S. warehouses.
The Sr. Supply Chain Specialist role is a 12-month maternity leave contract . The role allows for remote work in Ontario, Canada only . Travel may be required on occasion. Must be legally eligible for employment and reside in Ontario, Canada. The start date of this position will ideally begin in late September/early October of 2026 .

Since 2003, DIVA has introduced and onboarded millions of people as they keenly—or—anxiously—discovered reusable period care. Founded by mother-daughter duo Francine Chambers and Carinne Chambers-Saini, DIVA revolutionized the “feminine hygiene” industry and created the mass market adoption of sustainable period care alternatives. Today, the DIVA brand is synonymous with the menstrual care category, driving change and bringing sustainability to the forefront of new period care innovation.
We are DIVA.
Founded in 2002, DIVA disrupted the cycle care industry with the DivaCup®, offering a reusable, comfortable, and innovative alternative to disposable menstrual products.

As a pioneer in menstrual health and equity, DIVA has spent over two decades challenging taboos, advocating for education, and driving social impact initiatives that improve accessibility to period care worldwide. DIVA’s commitment to conscious wellness extends beyond menstrual care.

Guided by science-backed formulations and human-first innovation, DIVA continues to develop vegan, cruelty-free, and premium crafted products that
empower individuals to feel informed, confident, and cared for—without stigma.

Inventory Management & Forecasting Support inventory management, forecasting, and supply chain planning, including MRP, production scheduling, and monthly updates.
Monitor reconciliations, inventory counts, and adjustments across multiple warehouses in Canada and the U.S.
Assist in defining and tracking departmental KPIs to ensure inventory and supply chain efficiency.
Production & Assembly Coordination Collaborate with Sales and Marketing Communications to align production plans with demand forecasts.
Assist with assembly operations, coordinating with manufacturing partners to resolve production, inventory, or quality issues.
Participate in monthly production planning meetings with assembly partners (e.g., Unique Global) and provide status updates.
Purchasing & Vendor Management Support purchase orders, vendor quotes, work orders, and raw material approvals, ensuring cost efficiency and timely delivery.
Build and maintain relationships with suppliers, monitoring performance and holding vendors accountable for deliverables.
Assist with requests for quotes and support sourcing of raw materials as needed.
Cross-Functional Collaboration Partner with Accounting to reconcile MCOG accounts and support financial reporting related to supply chain operations.
Develop and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs) for supply chain and inventory management activities.
Support monthly reporting activities related to inventory and supply chain performance, and assist with proposal purchases for inventory to ensure product availability and alignment with business objectives.
Quality Assurance Support Collaborate with Quality Assurance to support the product realization process, investigate product issues, and implement corrective and preventative actions.
Identify opportunities for continual improvement across supply chain and assembly processes.
Ensure compliance with DIVA International Inc.’s ISO 13485 Quality Management System and B-Corp standards .
Qualifications: 3–5 years of experience in supply chain, inventory management, or operations analysis, preferably in CPG or regulated industries.
Strong analytical skills with experience in forecasting, MRP systems, and production planning.
Knowledge of inventory control, purchasing, and assembly operations.
Familiarity with quality management systems and regulatory requirements (ISO 13485, FDA, Health Canada).
Experience working with ERP systems (NetSuite or similar) and Excel (pivot tables, VLOOKUP).
Strong organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to collaborate effectively across departments and with external suppliers.
Detail-oriented, proactive, and able to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.

About Halter
At Halter, we’re on a mission to enable farmers and graziers to run the most productive and sustainable operations. Our customers are using Halter to break free from the time-intensive constraints of conventional practices. Imagine watching 500 cattle stand up and walk calmly towards their next break? No quad bikes, no dogs, no fences.

Just a group of cattle walking at their own pace. People say it looks like magic. Our customers are revolutionizing grazing with Halter. It's changing lives and transforming an industry. People join Halter to do meaningful work. By joining us you’ll be solving challenging problems within a talented team and a culture built for high performance.

Our team out-think, out-work and out-care. We’re committed to delivering real change in the world - this isn’t easy, and in truth, we love that it’s hard.
We’re backed to deliver on a mission that matters by Tier 1 investors including Founders Fund , Bessemer Venture Partners , BOND, DCVC , Blackbird , Promus Ventures , Rocket Lab’s Peter Beck and Icehouse ventures .
To find out more, visit our LinkedIn & Instagram .

Halter is scaling fast. More products, more customers, more complexity. That means a supply chain spanning contract manufacturing partners in Asia, a global component supplier base, and customers across global markets. We need someone to build it.
The Head of Supply Chain owns everything from demand signal to customer delivery. You'll lead the S&OP, supply planning, sourcing, and logistics functions, building a team and a supply chain that is fast, resilient, and capable of scaling with a company that is growing quickly across multiple hardware products and geographies.
This is a leadership role as much as a functional one. You'll spend as much time developing your team, building relationships across the business, and shaping how we operate as you will solving day-to-day supply chain problems. You'll work closely with our hardware, operations, commercial, and finance leadership to make sure the supply chain is never the constraint on Halter's growth.
You'll own the supply chain function. That means full accountability for performance across supply availability, cost, lead times, and logistics. And it means shaping the strategy, not just executing it.

Leadership and Team Development
Lead and develop the S&OP, supply planning, sourcing, and logistics functions, building a high-performing team that can scale with Halter.
Set a clear direction for the supply chain function, ensure every part of the team understands what they're accountable for, and hold a high bar on delivery.
Develop the people in your team. Invest in their growth, give them stretch and challenge, and build the depth of capability the function will need as Halter grows.
Build the culture of the supply chain team: high ownership, low ego, fast-moving, and deeply connected to the rest of the business.
S&OP and Integrated Planning
Own the S&OP process at Halter, ensuring we have a reliable, well-governed cadence that produces a reconciled demand and supply plan the business can commit to.
Drive alignment between commercial and operational teams on forecast, capacity, and supply position, making sure the right trade-offs are surfaced and resolved at pace.
Ensure the supply chain always has a clear forward view of demand, and that supply plans are proactively adjusted before gaps become crises.
Sourcing and Supplier Management
Own the sourcing strategy across Halter's supply base, ensuring we have the right suppliers, the right commercial terms, and the right relationships to support our growth.
Build a supplier base that is resilient, competitive, and capable of scaling with us, reducing single-source dependency and geographic concentration where it creates unacceptable risk.
Develop strong, trust-based relationships with key suppliers and ensure supplier performance is actively managed against clear expectations.
Lead commercial negotiations on major supply agreements, with a focus on total cost of ownership, lead time, and supply security.
Supply Planning and Inventory
Ensure we have a supply planning function that translates demand into accurate material requirements, maintains healthy inventory positions, and keeps purchase orders moving reliably through the supply chain.
Own inventory strategy across the portfolio, balancing availability against working capital and ensuring the business always has a clear picture of stock position and risk.
Identify and resolve structural issues in how we plan supply before they become operational problems.
Logistics
Own the end-to-end logistics function, ensuring product moves from our manufacturing partners to our customers efficiently, reliably, and at the right cost.
Build and manage relationships with freight and logistics partners, ensuring service levels are met and costs are competitive.
Develop a logistics strategy that can scale with Halter's geographic expansion and growing product portfolio, including customs, compliance, and in-country distribution.
Strategy and Cross-Functional Leadership
Own the supply chain strategy for Halter, defining the roadmap for how we build a supply chain that is a genuine competitive advantage as we scale.
Work closely with hardware, operations, commercial, and finance leadership to ensure the supply chain is aligned to the business strategy and never the constraint on growth.
Collaborate with the Operations Delivery Lead on NPI and sustaining programme delivery, ensuring the supply chain is set up to support every product launch, change and volume ramp.

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.
The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.
At Flexport, we are building the unified Supply Chain Operating System for global trade. While traditional consulting firms deliver slide decks and walk away, Flexport’s Forward Deployed Consultants (FDCs) embed directly on the operational frontline alongside enterprise clients to architect, build, and deploy real-time supply chain solutions.
Operating alongside a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE), you are a senior technical subject matter expert sitting at the intersection of Operations Research, data science, supply chain strategy, and executive client delivery. You will embed with Fortune 500 retailers, high-tech manufacturers, and global brand leadership to audit complex logistics networks, identify multi-million-dollar cost leaks, and build executable optimization models that transform client supply chains.
You will serve as the solution design lead across a set of Flexport capabilities:
Order, booking, and shipment management
Transportation planning, consolidation, and exception management
Data integrations, workflow automation, and operational analytics
You won't just analyze data in a vacuum: you will write Python scripts, design supply chain algorithms, whiteboard architectures with C-suite leaders, and deploy live automated workflows that optimize cargo moving across ocean, air, and land networks.
You Will
Embed & Audit: Deploy directly to client headquarters and logistics hubs to map physical and digital processes, audit supply chain data, uncover root-cause bottlenecks, and quantify hard-dollar ROI across freight, tariffs, and inventory.
Architect Optimization Models: Design, prototype, and scale mathematical supply chain models using Python, SQL, and proprietary tools. Focus on mode mix planning, 3D origin bin-packing, container payload balancing, dynamic safety stock, and supplier consolidation.
Lead Solution Design & Product Integration: Serve as the technical solution design lead across Flexport capabilities (Order & Shipment Management, Transportation Planning, Data Integration). Partner with FDEs and core engineering teams to turn your mathematical models into production workflows inside the Flexport Control Tower and Workflows platform.
Drive Executive Strategy & Proposals: Partner with commercial teams to co-create high-impact client proposals. Translate complex data models into clear business stories, presenting ROI projections directly to executive stakeholders (COOs, CFOs, VPs of Supply Chain).
Bridge Strategy & Frontline Execution: Work side-by-side with frontline operations teams at ports, cross-docks, and client sites to validate models in live workflows, collect operational feedback, and ensure lasting adoption.
Own End-to-End Program Workstreams: Manage 90-day deployment sprints from start to finish—building project roadmaps, running data pipelines, eliminating roadblocks, and delivering measurable results against aggressive timelines.
Measure Financial & Environmental Impact: Rigorously monitor project metrics, measuring hard-dollar cost reductions (demurrage saved, modal savings, etc)
Productize Field Insights: Identify root causes of logistics losses, build reusable playbooks, and partner with product managers to transform solutions into permanent platform features.
You Should Have
Educational Background: BA/BS or higher in Industrial Engineering, Operations Research, Computer Science, Applied Physics, Supply Chain, or a related technical field.
Supply Chain & Logistics Expertise: 6+ years of professional experience in senior/staff roles in supply chain management/consulting, product management, logistics engineering, or freight forwarding.
Technical & Analytical: Proficiency in Python, SQL, and data visualization tools (Looker, Tableau).
Mathematical Modeling & Systems Thinking: Proven ability for systems-thinking to build decision-support systems, reason about end-to-end physical dependencies, and handle imperfect enterprise data.
Technical Program Management: Demonstrated success overseeing project workstreams from problem definition through setting goals, prototyping, delivery management, risk management, adoption, and impact measurement.
Executive Communication & Influence: Outstanding interpersonal skills with the ability to whiteboard complex workflows, build deep trust with technical and business stakeholders, and push back constructively on the status quo.
Frontline Grit: Willingness to get your hands dirty learning ground operations on-site at ports, warehouses, and client logistics hubs.
Mindset: Self-starter mentality, comfortable navigating high ambiguity, with a relentless bias toward action and value delivery. Strong attention to detail and proficient problem solving skills.

We are seeking a Demand Planner – North America Retail to support the regional demand and inventory strategy for Ōura’s North America retail business across key partners including Best Buy, Amazon, Target, Costco, Canada, and other strategic accounts.
In this individual contributor role, you will own core forecasting, replenishment planning, and inventory analysis for North America retail. You will translate point-of-sale, inventory, promotional, and commercial signals into clear demand plans and actionable recommendations. You will partner closely with Retail, GTM, Supply Planning, Finance, and Product to improve forecast quality, support launches and promotions, and help maintain healthy in-channel inventory.
This role is ideal for someone who is strong in detail, comfortable working across large and imperfect data sets, and excited to help build more scalable planning processes as Ōura’s retail business continues to grow.

North America Retail Forecasting & Planning
Build and maintain weekly, monthly, and quarterly sell-through and sell-in forecasts for North America retail partners.
Translate retailer POS, inventory positions, historical trends, seasonality, promotional plans, and new product introductions into demand assumptions and forecast updates.
Support the monthly consensus planning process by preparing inputs, highlighting key changes, and identifying risks and opportunities.
Maintain a clear view of baseline demand, upside, downside, and key forecast drivers across retail accounts.
Help develop and refine planning logic, assumptions, and planning cadences for retail accounts as the business scales.
Inventory Management & Replenishment Support
Monitor retail inventory health using on-hand inventory, on-order inventory, weeks-of-supply, and forward-looking demand.
Recommend sell-in and replenishment plans that balance revenue goals, service levels, and inventory health.
Identify risk areas such as low stock, excess inventory, phase-in and phase-out transitions, and launch constraints, and escalate issues with clear recommendations.
Support allocation decisions during constrained supply periods by quantifying demand, inventory risk, and business impact.
Partner with Supply Planning and Retail teams to improve in-stock position and reduce avoidable lost sales.
Launches, Promotions & Cross-Functional Execution
Partner with Retail, GTM, Product, and Supply Planning on promotional events, assortment changes, and new retailer, product, or door launches.
Convert commercial plans into forecast assumptions and planning scenarios.
Support new product launch planning and lifecycle transitions by helping track assumptions, timing, and ramp expectations.
Contribute to end-of-life planning by helping assess inventory exposure, markdown risk, and timing shifts.
Reporting, Analytics & Continuous Improvement
Own recurring retail demand planning analyses and reporting, including forecast versus actuals, trend views, and inventory health metrics.
Analyze weekly and monthly performance to explain what happened, why it happened, and what should change in the next plan.
Maintain a transparent audit trail of forecast changes and their impact to units, revenue, and inventory.
Build and improve tools and reporting in Google Sheets, Tableau, or similar platforms so stakeholders can focus on decisions rather than manual data gathering.
Help shape business requirements and validate outputs for planning system improvements, including retail forecasting and inventory workflows.
Support process improvement work-streams that make retail planning more scalable, accurate, and decision-oriented.

4–6+ years of hands-on demand planning, merchandise planning, or related analytical experience supporting physical products in retail, consumer electronics, CPG, or similar environments.
Experience working with retail forecasting concepts such as sell-through versus sell-in, promotional lifts, inventory targets, and weeks-of-supply.
Strong analytical and modeling skills, including advanced proficiency in Excel and/or Google Sheets.
Comfort working with large data sets from multiple sources, including POS, inventory, and shipment data.
Ability to translate analysis into clear business insights, including key drivers, risks, trade-offs, and recommendations.
Experience working cross-functionally with commercial, supply chain, finance, and product stakeholders.
Strong ownership mindset with the ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
Excellent communication skills and the ability to influence decisions through strong analysis and clear storytelling.

Experience with planning tools such as Pigment, Anaplan, o9, Blue Yonder, Relex, or similar platforms.
Experience with BI tools such as Tableau, Looker, or Power BI.
Background in consumer electronics, wearables, premium hardware, or other multi-channel physical product businesses.
Experience supporting new retail launches, new assortments, or retail expansion into new doors or countries.
Familiarity with S&OP or IBP processes and preparation of materials for leadership reviews.
Success in This Role
You create reliable retail demand plans that improve alignment across Retail, Supply Planning, Finance, and GTM.
You help the team make faster, clearer decisions by connecting data to business actions.
You proactively identify demand and inventory risks and bring forward practical recommendations.

We are seeking a Senior Logistics Coordinator to join the Australia logistics function within Deployment Operations. This role is central to the coordination and execution of Anduril Australia's international and domestic freight operations, with a strong emphasis on carrier management, international freight coordination, and operational visibility across all modes of transport.
Working alongside the Senior Logistics Manager, you will take ownership of day-to-day freight coordination while contributing to carrier strategy, KPI reporting, and process development. You will coordinate closely with Anduril's Compliance function on trade compliance matters, working alongside customs brokers and internal teams to ensure all shipments meet regulatory requirements including ITAR, AQIS, and ABF.
This is a high-impact role in a lean, fast-growing team. You will operate with significant autonomy and have a direct line of sight to the function's strategic direction. For the right candidate, this role offers a clear development path toward senior logistics leadership within Anduril Australia.

International & Domestic Freight Coordination
— Coordinate end-to-end shipment execution across all modes: road (LTL/FTL), air, ocean, and parcel — both international and domestic
— Manage carrier booking, scheduling, and performance tracking across the Anduril Australia freight network
— Ensure freight documentation is complete, accurate, and compliant for all shipments
— Monitor shipment exceptions, delays, and escalations; drive corrective actions and communicate proactively with stakeholders
— Coordinate with 3PL providers, freight forwarders, and last-mile carriers to ensure on-time, in-full delivery performance
Trade Compliance Coordination
— Coordinate with Anduril's Compliance function on import/export requirements for all international shipments
— Work with customs brokers to ensure shipments comply with AQIS, ABF, and biosecurity requirements
— Support the Compliance team on ITAR-controlled shipments, export licences, and classified material handling from a logistics execution perspective
— Maintain accurate shipping documentation and audit-ready logistics records
— Support customs audits, broker reviews, and regulatory reporting as required by the Compliance function
Analytics, Reporting & Cost Management
— Track and report on logistics KPIs: cost per shipment, on-time delivery, transit time, carrier reliability, claims rate
— Analyse freight spend data to identify cost drivers, savings opportunities, and efficiency improvements
— Maintain and develop logistics dashboards and reporting cadences (weekly operational, monthly executive)
— Support monthly freight accruals, invoice reconciliation, and financial reporting
— Contribute to carrier benchmarking, rate analysis, and RFP processes
Carrier & Stakeholder Management
— Build and maintain operational relationships with key carriers, freight forwarders, and 3PL providers
— Manage lane rates, routing guides, and carrier assignments within TMS/ERP systems
— Collaborate cross-functionally with Supply Chain, Programs, Finance, and Procurement teams
— Support carrier strategy development alongside the Senior Logistics Manager
Process Development & Continuous Improvement
— Develop and maintain standard operating procedures and logistics playbooks for the Australia function
— Identify and implement process improvements to streamline operations, reduce cost, and enhance service quality
— Conduct root-cause analysis of shipment exceptions, claims, and compliance incidents
— Contribute to TMS/ERP system optimisation and data quality initiatives

— Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, Logistics, International Trade, Business, or related field
— 5–7 years of progressive experience in logistics, freight, transportation, or supply chain management
— Demonstrated experience with international freight operations, including import/export processes
— Working knowledge of Australian customs and biosecurity requirements (AQIS, ABF) and international trade compliance
— Experience with multi-modal freight management: road, air, ocean, and parcel
— Proficiency in TMS and/or ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, NetSuite, or similar)
— Strong analytical skills with experience in Excel, data analysis, and KPI reporting
— Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and cross-functional collaboration skills
— Ability to work autonomously in a lean, fast-paced, high-growth environment
— Ability to obtain and maintain an Australian Government security clearance (NV1/NV2)

— Experience in defence, aerospace, or high-technology environments
— Familiarity with ITAR and export control regulations
— Experience with dangerous goods / hazardous materials shipping
— Exposure to Lean/Six Sigma or continuous improvement methodologies
— Experience with data visualisation tools (Power BI, Tableau, or similar)
— Experience managing customs broker and freight forwarder relationships
— Postgraduate qualification in Supply Chain, International Trade, or MBA

s.h: Our client is looking for a Logistics Coordinator.
s.t:
Our client operates within the international trade and logistics sector, supporting global supply chain operations through freight coordination, import/export documentation, and transportation management. Over the past several years, they have continued expanding their logistics capabilities while supporting customers across multiple international markets.
The Logistics Coordinator will play a critical role in managing ocean and air freight shipments from booking through final documentation. This position requires exceptional organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to coordinate effectively with carriers, warehouses, suppliers, and internal stakeholders to ensure smooth shipment execution.

Request and compare ocean and air freight quotations based on cost, transit times, routing options, and service levels.
Coordinate bookings with carriers, freight forwarders, warehouses, suppliers, and customers.
Monitor shipment progress and track key milestones from origin to destination.
Coordinate container loading schedules, pickups, and transportation logistics.
Review and verify Bills of Lading, Air Waybills, shipping instructions, and release documentation.
Prepare, review, and maintain export documentation, including Commercial Invoices, Packing Lists, Certificates of Origin, Health Certificates, Certificates of Free Sale, and other required documents.
Ensure all shipping documentation is accurate, complete, and compliant with international trade requirements.
Communicate shipment updates and proactively address delays, discrepancies, or operational issues.
Work closely with internal teams and external partners to ensure smooth shipment execution.
Maintain organized records of shipments, documentation, and freight-related communications.
Support continuous improvement of logistics processes and operational efficiency.
Manage multiple shipments simultaneously while meeting deadlines and maintaining attention to detail.

Experience coordinating international ocean and air freight shipments.
Knowledge of import/export processes and logistics operations.
Familiarity with export documentation and shipping compliance requirements.
Strong communication skills with the ability to collaborate across multiple departments and external partners.
Ability to manage multiple shipments simultaneously while meeting deadlines.
High level of attention to detail and organization.
Strong problem-solving and follow-up skills.

Previous experience in logistics, freight forwarding, supply chain, transportation, or international trade.
Understanding of Bills of Lading, Air Waybills, Certificates of Origin, and related export documentation.
Experience working with freight carriers, customs brokers, warehouses, and freight forwarders.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Outlook.
Ability to work independently while maintaining strong communication with leadership and team members.
English proficiency required.

Full-Time position.
100% Remote.
Opportunity to work directly with executive leadership.
Exposure to international logistics and global trade operations.
Collaborative and fast-paced work environment.

Responsibilities of the Procurement Specialist may include but will not be limited to: Contracting and Procurement Management: Serve as a contracting officer responsible for primarily purchasing consumable and automation supplies, equipment, and services.

Process purchase orders for goods and services from government and non-government sources using the judiciary's financial management system. Coordinate with court financial staff to verify authorization and availability of funds prior to processing purchase requests.

Develop and maintain tracking systems for funds commitments, obligations, and expenditures. Track and process subscription renewals, cancellations, and transfers. Review and process travel authorizations, obligate travel funds, and approval central court travel requests.

Research and evaluate suppliers based on price, quality, selection, service reliability, and compliance with federal procurement requirements. Track delivery of goods and services, following up on outstanding orders to ensure timely receipt. Assist with contract administration, including clarifying requirements, resolving conflicts, and monitoring vendor performance. Plan and coordinate time and delivery of purchases.

As a Senior Technical Procurement Specialist – PCBs / Electronics , you are responsible for the end-to-end procurement of printed circuit boards (PCBs) through our manufacturing partners (Contract Manufacturers, CMs). You work at the interface between Engineering, Supply Chain, and Production, translating technical requirements into clear supplier packages, negotiating costs and lead times, and ensuring that the right boards are available on time and at the required quality level.
This role is ideal for someone who understands how PCBs are actually manufactured (stack-ups, materials, tolerances, DFM) and enjoys the commercial and operational aspects of bringing products to life at scale.

s.h: What is your Day to Day Mission
s.t:
Own PCB procurement end-to-end – from RFQ and quote analysis through PO creation, order tracking, delivery, and closure.
Translate engineering needs into supplier-ready data – review BOMs, Gerbers, stackups, drawings, and specifications to ensure CMs have complete and correct information.
Manage contract manufacturers – build strong relationships, align on capabilities and capacity, and drive performance on cost, quality, lead time, and responsiveness, including on-site visits of contract manufacturers
Optimize cost and lead time – run competitive RFQs, analyze trade-offs (volume, lead time, technology level), and negotiate pricing and terms with CMs.
Mitigate supply and technical risks – monitor material availability (e.g. laminates, copper weights, finishes), propose alternates, and escalate issues before they become schedule slips.
Support NPI and engineering changes – coordinate production ramp-up, manage ECO impacts on PCB procurement, and ensure smooth transitions from prototype to volume.
Ensure quality and compliance – work closely with QA/engineering to address nonconformances, track supplier performance, and ensure boards meet required standards (e.g. IPC, customer specs).
Keep everything organized and visible – maintain accurate data in ERP/MRP and tracking tools, provide clear status updates, and keep stakeholders aligned on dates and risks.

s.h: What you bring to the team
s.t:
Technical background in electronics or PCBs – ability to read schematics, BOMs, and Gerber/ODB++ files; familiarity with PCB stackups, materials, finishes, and manufacturing constraints.
Experience in electronics/PCB procurement or supply chain – ideally working directly with PCB fabs and/or PCB assembly contract manufacturers.
Comfortable working with engineers – you can discuss layer counts, impedance, controlled tolerances, and DFM/DFT topics and translate that into supplier requirements.
Strong commercial and negotiation skills – able to compare quotes, build cost breakdowns, negotiate pricing and MOQs, and structure win–win agreements.
Data-driven and detail-oriented – you spot inconsistencies in BOMs/specs, track multiple orders in parallel, and use data (lead times, yields, costs) to drive decisions.
Tool-savvy – experience with Netsuit ERP/MRP systems and common engineering tools (e.g. Altium/KiCad/Cadence exports, Excel/Sheets for analysis, ticketing/project tools for tracking).
Collaborative communicator – clear written and verbal communication with suppliers and internal teams; able to summarize complex situations into actionable updates both in English and German.
Bias for execution – you’re proactive, take ownership of issues, and push to resolution when schedules and builds are at risk.
Familiarity with PLM and configuration management (ECR/ECO), supplier qualification, FAI (AS9102), and quality documentation.
Clear, concise communication and the ability to lead cross-functional reviews and drive decisions in a fast-moving environment.

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.
Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.
Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

Work on a civilisation-scale problem - Clean, baseload fusion energy is one of the few genuinely world-changing challenges, and every hire in Finance, People, or Legal directly accelerates the path to a working stellarator.
Grow as fast as the company does - With headcount set to roughly 5x in a few years and major technical milestones ahead on the path to our demo machine and first power plant, your role grows under you; today's hire is tomorrow's function lead.
Tackle problems that don't exist elsewhere - Fusion sits at a rare intersection of deep-tech R&D, industrial procurement, government relations, and venture financing, so non-tech functions face challenges no other workplace can offer.

You will play a central role in capturing those learnings and translating them into the supplier strategies that will underpin a heating system capable of driving a commercial stellarator.

Using your extensive domain expertise in one of the common heating systems used in fusion today, you will drive delivery of the high power Radio Frequency and particle sources being developed by Proxima’s partners.
Evaluation of vendor proposals and designs to determine the optimal path to efficiently deliver power to the Alpha stellarator.
Draw from and contribute to our stellarator design process by integrating the system being developed within the Proxima supply chain with the wider Alpha stellarator and the teams delivering them.

Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to articulate complex technical concepts clearly to non-experts.

Zurich Instruments is a technology leader in advanced test and measurement instruments and in control electronics for quantum computing. Our products are used in many challenging research fields by scientists all over the world and by leading high-tech companies worldwide. We help advance science and build the next generation of quantum computers.
As Senior Supply & Production Planner, you own the link between demand and the availability of material and capacity. You translate forecast and order-driven demand into procurement plans with our suppliers, convert confirmed demand into an executable production plan, and anticipate capacity gaps on a rolling 6-month horizon.

You work at the interface between Supply Chain, Manufacturing, Business Fulfillment, R&D and our suppliers, and are the single point of reference for the question "when can we build and ship this?"

Translate the rolling demand forecast for series-production line into a 3–6 month procurement plan with suppliers, and maintain planning parameters (lead times, safety stocks, reorder points, lot sizes) in the ERP.
Build procurement plan for our project-based business, identify long-lead components for preventive purchase before order intake, and quantify each commitment for approval.
Run the MRP cycle, convert requirements into purchase orders, and track material readiness by project, escalating delivery risks early.
Issue the weekly production plan, create and drive manufacturing orders, and coordinate internal logistics so material is picked and staged on time.
Keep planning master data (BOMs, routings, work centre capacities) accurate with Manufacturing Engineering and R&D, and confirm feasible dates to Business Fulfillment and Sales.
Evaluate production capacity on a rolling 6‑month horizon, flag bottlenecks early, and propose measures such as load leveling, build‑ahead, or outsourcing.
Own planning processes in the ERP and report key KPIs: on-time delivery, material shortages, inventory coverage, forecast accuracy, and capacity load.
Your profile
Technical or commercial education (HF, FH or BSc) in supply chain, industrial engineering or a comparable field; a planning certification (e.g. APICS CPIM) is an advantage.
5-10 years' planning experience in a high-mix / low-volume electronics or precision instrumentation environment.
Solid ERP planning skills: MRP (Material Requirements Planning) and MPS (Master Production Scheduling), manufacturing orders and capacity planning; experience with Odoo is an advantage.
Comfortable working with both forecast-driven and order-driven project planning logic in parallel.
Strong analytical skills, confident with data and Excel.
Able to take decisions under uncertainty, and to substantiate a "no" with facts.
Clear communicator across manufacturing, supply chain, sales and suppliers.
Fluent English; German is a big advantage.
We offer a diverse work environment with an open and transparent company culture where personal development forms the basis of our success. We thrive on cooperation and support distributed decision-making that allows everyone to take responsibility and generate substantial impact from the start and on many levels.

For an international pharmaceutical environment, we are looking for an experienced Manager Supply Chain Site Coordinator for a 12\-month temporary assignment based in Boudry.
The key focus of this position is to act as the central Supply Chain interface between internal Planning teams and external Contract Manufacturing Organizations (CMOs).
You will coordinate the flow of supply and demand information between both sides and ensure that production plans, purchase orders, forecasts and delivery schedules are aligned with market requirements. A major part of the role is to proactively identify and manage supply exceptions, shortages and backorders and to ensure that potential disruptions are addressed before they impact Customer Service Levels and product availability.
This is therefore not a general Supply Chain position, but a highly collaborative and operational coordination role at the intersection of Planning, External Manufacturing and market supply.

Coordinate supply and demand requirements between internal stakeholders and manufacturing partners
Ensure adequate production at CMOs to meet customer and market demand
Manage and follow up on Purchase Orders, ensuring timely placement, confirmation and delivery
Closely monitor delivery schedules, open orders and order exceptions
Provide forecasts to CMOs and align production requirements with medium\- and long\-term demand
Proactively identify potential supply disruptions, shortages, allocations, backorders and stock\-outs
Assess the impact of supply or quality\-related issues on market availability and coordinate appropriate actions
Manage supply priorities and exceptions to maintain agreed Customer Service Levels
Support synchronization between customer orders, production campaigns and material availability
Act as a key contact for product inquiries, shipments, scheduling and logistics\-related topics
Work cross\-functionally with Market Supply Planning, Customer Service, Quality, Manufacturing Technology, Procurement and external manufacturing partners
Support supply chain performance analysis and relevant KPIs
Coordinate product rework/redress activities at CMO sites where required
Support and lead supply chain\-related projects as needed

Hands\-on experience in supply planning and coordination with manufacturing sites and/or external manufacturing partners
Strong knowledge of Master Scheduling, Forecasting, Customer Service, Logistics, Distribution and/or Inventory Management
Very good understanding of operational planning processes, including MPS, MRP and forecasting

Excellent MS Excel and MS Office skills
Fluent English; French and/or German would be an advantage
Willingness to travel occasionally if required

We are particularly interested in candidates who have worked in a complex pharmaceutical supply chain environment and are comfortable coordinating supply activities across Planning teams, manufacturing sites and external partners.

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.
Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.
Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

s.h: BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO
s.t:
Build the machine that builds the machine . Join TechOps at the forefront of advanced manufacturing, we’re building the production system that will enable commercial fusion. The Production lines, tooling, and processes are being developed from the ground up; you'll create the ways of working, not inherit them.
Work at the frontier of manufacturing technology . Bring your creativity to evaluate, qualify, and deploy processes with no industry playbook, every component you build and every process you shape goes directly into the core of the stellarator magnet technology.
Do work that matters, and see it grow . The hardware you build is the product and your career grows with it, from prototyping and process development through quality and industrialization, alongside exceptional colleagues from around the world.
Make an impact you can point to . In a small, fast-moving team, your calls on equipment, quality, and process directly shape how a world-class deep-tech company produces superconducting magnets with results visible on the shop floor, not buried in a slidedeck.

Build and maintain medium- to long-term production plans that align engineering, procurement, and manufacturing.
Balance capacity, material availability, and evolving engineering requirements to enable predictable execution.
Identify and resolve constraints before they affect day-to-day production on the manufacturing floor.
Support the successful delivery of critical fusion hardware while improving efficiency, coordination, and transparency across manufacturing operations.

Translate project milestones into detailed, resourced and executable manufacturing plans.
Perform capacity planning and balance workloads across internal and external manufacturing resources.
Coordinate with the Procurement & Logistics Department to optimize inventory availability, minimize shortages and support efficient material flow across manufacturing.
Anticipate the impact of evolving engineering requirements and material constraints on the production plan and adjust proactively ahead of execution.
Work closely with Manufacturing Engineering to incorporate process changes into production plans.
Partner with Program Managers to align production priorities with program objectives.
Analyze production performance data to identify risks to material availability, capacity and delivery timelines, feeding findings back into the plan.
Monitor planning-level metrics such as capacity utilization and lead times and use them to continuously improve the accuracy of the production plan.
Support the design, implementation and continuous improvement of production planning systems and processes, contributing to the selection and deployment of future ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning)/MRP (Material Requirements Planning) capabilities.
Contribute to the development of scalable production planning processes as Proxima transitions from prototype manufacturing to industrial deployment.

You have a degree in Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations Management or a related field, or equivalent practical experience in production planning, manufacturing operations or supply chain within a complex engineering environment (aerospace, fusion, automotive, energy or other high-tech manufacturing industries).
You have experience with production planning systems, MRP/ERP workflows and manufacturing data management and are excited by the opportunity to help implement and shape planning tools in a rapidly growing manufacturing organization.
You think in terms of capacity, material flow and constraints and you are comfortable modeling trade-offs before they become execution problems.
You thrive in fast-paced, dynamic environments where priorities evolve quickly and planning decisions have a direct impact on manufacturing execution.
You communicate effectively across multidisciplinary teams and can balance competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
You are proactive, detail-oriented and comfortable working in an evolving hardware development environment.

We are looking for a Senior Materials Planner to join our Supply Chain and Inventory team in Oxford. You would be working closely with engineering, manufacturing and procurement to make sure the right parts arrive when the build needs them.
Our engineering builds and New Product Introduction programmes move at the pace of the parts that arrive. When a single long lead item slips, a build slot sits idle and the schedule behind it shifts. Today the picture of what is on order, what is late and what that does to the next build lives in several places at once, across MRP data, vendor conversations and spreadsheets. Nobody owns the whole picture, and that is the job.
You will run system level materials planning from MRP data, turning forecast into a build schedule people can rely on. You will source and negotiate with vendors, raise purchase requisitions and chase deliveries that are drifting. A good deal of this role is telling people early that a date has moved.
This is an in office role in Oxford, five days a week. Materials planning here depends on being close to the builds, the stores and the people running them.
In this position, you will have the opportunity to improve material availability, accelerate production timelines and strengthen supply chain reliability across engineering and NPI programmes.

s.h: Your key responsibilities can be split into two categories
s.t:
Planning and scheduling
Execute system level materials planning from MRP data to support engineering builds and NPI schedules
Publish and maintain daily and weekly build schedules from forecast analysis and material availability
Monitor, report and resolve material shortages, discrepancies and constraints before they stop a build
Manage production work orders and report on material readiness and build progress
Vendor and supply
Source and negotiate with vendors, including obtaining quotes and agreeing lead times
Raise purchase requisitions and expedite deliveries that are slipping
Act as the point of contact between vendors and the internal teams waiting on parts
Work across engineering, manufacturing and procurement to clear blockers on critical builds

To be successful, you will need five or more years of materials planning in a manufacturing environment with multi level bills of materials, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

You will have a working command of MRP across planning, purchasing, inventory and manufacturing operations, hands on experience with ERP and PLM systems, and the confidence to analyse large sets of data and act on what they tell you.

You will need to lead cross functional work, speak plainly to vendors and internal teams alike, and operate with urgency in an environment where priorities move.
